Resumen: The facts of the case concern the forced disappearance, torture and extrajudicial execution of Heliodoro Portugal, detained on May 14, 1979, while the country was governed by a military regime. The facts also concern the failure of the State to investigate, identify and convict those responsible. The remains of Heliodoro Portugal were found in September 1999 in military barracks, although only in 2001 was it confirmed with absolute certainty that these remains pertained to him. The IA Court reiterated its jurisprudence regarding the special characteristics and the continued character of the crime of forced disappearance. Similarly, the IA Court assessed if the classification of the crime of forced disappearance in domestic law was appropriate to the requirements and minimum elements as stipulated by international human rights law.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the illegal and arbitrary detention of Yvon Neptune, who served as Prime Minister of Haiti, for his responsibility of the massacre of the population of La Scierie and of the fire in various houses in February 2004. Resumen: The facts of the case concern the extrajudicial execution of Wilmer Zambrano, Segundo Olmedo and José Miguel Caicedo in March 1993, and the lack of investigation and punishment of those responsible. The victims were executed during an operation carried out by the Ecuadoran Armed Forces and the National Police. The events occurred in the context of a climate of insecurity and internal commotion, which lead to the ordering of Decree N° 86 on September 3, 1992 by the President of the Republic, which commanded the intervention of the armed forces. The IA Court established standards on the scope of the suspension of guarantees in states of exception, as well as criteria for the legitimate use of force on the part of state security forces.

Title: Boyce y otros
CorteIDH: Boyce y otros y Dacosta Cadogan. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 14 de noviembre de 2017|Boyce y otros y Dacosta Cadogan. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 21 de noviembre de 2011|Boyce y otros. Sentencia de 20 de noviembre de 2007|Boyce y otros. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 9 de marzo de 2020
Resumen: The facts of the present case refer to the mandatory sentencing of four people to the death penalty for the crime of homicide. The IA Court developed standards regarding the incompatibility of the mandatory imposition of the death sentence with the right to life and prohibition of the arbitrary violation of life. Additionally, the Court analyzed the conditions of detention in light of the prohibition of cruel, inhumane and degrading treatment.

Title: Chaparro Álvarez y Lapo Íñiguez
CorteIDH: Chaparro Alvarez y Lapo Iñíguez. Sentencia de 26 de noviembre de 2008|Chaparro Alvarez y Lapo Iñiguez. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 27 de enero de 2015|Chaparro Álvarez y Lapo Íñiguez. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 19 de mayo de 2010|Chaparro Álvarez y Lapo Íñiguez. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 22 de febrero de 2011|Chaparro Alvarez y Lapo Íñiguez. CIDH: Chaparro Alvarez y Lapo Iniguez. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 77/03
Lugar de los hechos: Chaparro Álvarez y Lapo Íñiguez: 2° 8' 53" S, 79° 52' 55" W
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the illegal and arbitrary detention of Chilean national Juan Carlos Chaparro Álvarez, owner of the “Aislantes Plumavit Compañía Limitada” factory, and Ecuadorian national Freddy Hernán Lapo Íñiguez, the factory manager. These detentions were carried out in November 1997, in the context of “Operación Antinarcótica Rivera”, an operation under which cool-boxes similar to those produced in the factory of the victims were seized if the presence of cocaine hydrochloride and heroine within them had been detected. The IA Court developed standards regarding preventive detention and the effectiveness of available legal resources to challenge said detention. The Court also stressed that decisions adopted by internal organisms which could affect human rights must be duly justified. Failure to do so renders them arbitrary. The Court established that the condition for ensuring the right to defense is the motivation of the judicial decision. In this case, the lack of motivation impeded the defense’s ability to be made aware of the reasons why the victims were deprived of their liberty, and hindered the task of presenting new evidence or arguments to achieve their liberation or challenge, in a more effective manner, the determining evidence against them. The IA Court also developed standards regarding the adoption of real precautionary measures with regards to the right to property.

Title: Pueblo Saramaka
CorteIDH: Pueblo Saramaka. Resolución del Presidente de la CorteIDH de 20 de abril de 2010|Saramaka. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 4 de septiembre de 2013|Saramaka. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 23 de noviembre de 2011|Saramaka. Sentencia de 12 de agosto de 2008|Saramaka. Sentencia de 28 de noviembre de 2007
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to failure on the part of the State to take effective measures for the recognition and protection of the right to use and enjoy territories traditionally occupied by the Saramaka Community, as a result of exploitation and exploration projects on the part of private companies in said territories. The IA Court established standards regarding the conditions for the legitimate restriction of the rights to ancestral territory, particularly with regard to the relationship between natural resources and subsistence as a community. Similarly, the Court established standards regarding the obligation of the State to guarantee the right of consultation.

Sentencia de 4 de julio de 2007|Escue Zapata. Resolución del Presidente de 8 de febrero de 2012
Resumen: The facts of the case provide an account of the verbal and physical violence, the unsubstantiated accusation of being a guerrilla fighter, the illegal raid of residence and the subsequent extrajudicial execution of indigenous leader Germán Escué Zapata, member of the indigenous reserve of Jambaló, Paez del Norte del Cauca community. These acts were perpetrated by members of the National Army on February 1, 1988. The Colombian State partially recognized its responsibility for the events, and admitted that members of the public forces illegally detained Escué, who was beaten and subsequently extrajudicially executed. The State also acknowledged that there had not been an effective investigation. The IA Court developed standards regarding illegal search and entry of places of residence, considering this an arbitrary and abusive interference of the home and a violation of family and private life for those people who are affected.

Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the torture suffered by Uruguayan national Juan Francisco Bueno Alves, at the hands of members of the Argentine Federal Police. This was carried out with the intention of making him declare against himself and his lawyer. Following these events, judicial proceedings lasting more than 9 years began and were finished without the identification and subsequent trial of those responsible having been established. The IA Court established the importance if prompt investigation in cases involving allegations of torture or mistreatment, particularly when there are no witnesses.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the limitations on the right to property of the Salvador Chiriboga brothers, imposed by the Municipal Council of Quito. In May 1991, the Municipal Council declared an estate of 60 hectares to be of public utility, with the objective of expropriation and urgent occupation. The IA Court carried out an analysis regarding the restrictions to private property in a democratic society. The Court then established guiding criteria for said restrictions, which ensure the minimum possible interference with the effective exercise of rights. These criteria include public utility, social interest, and the payment of fair, adequate, prompt, and effective compensation.

CIDH: Masacre de la Rochela. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 42/02
Lugar de los hechos: Masacre de la Rochela: 5° 5' 10" N, 75° 41' 23" W
Resumen: The facts of this case relate to the massacre of a group of 15 judicial officials who were members of a Judicial Commission (Unidad Móvil de Investigación) who were performing their duties by carrying out an investigation into the massacre of 19 traders and other occurrences of violence in the region of Magdalena Medio. Of the 15 victims, 12 were executed and 3 survived. The IA Court established State responsibility for the actions committed by paramilitary groups in the context of expansion and territorial control against guerrilla insurgents and noted the particular severity of the events that resulted in the intimidation of the judicial officials dedicated to investigating serious human rights’ violations. The IA Court developed standards relating to the violation of the right to life of the 3 survivors, since they survived purely due to fortuitous circumstances, even though they had been dealt “the final blow”. Furthermore it analyzed the lack of investigation and impunity of the acts in relation to the standard of due diligence.

Lugar de los hechos: Cantoral Huamaní y García Santa Cruz: 12° 4' 10" S, 77° 2' 58" W
Geolocalización de los hechos del caso: Cantoral Huamaní y García Santa Cruz
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the kidnapping and subsequent torture and extrajudicial execution of Saúl Isaac Cantoral Huamaní and Consuelo Trinidad García Santa Cruz, both trade union leaders associated with mining. The IA Court considered that during the 80s and towards the end of 2000, Peru experienced a conflict between armed groups and military and police agents. This conflict was exacerbated by the systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. The IA Court evidenced the repression focusing on trade union leaders, highlighting the State’s obligation to investigate these types of crimes effectively and with due diligence, given the intimidating effect of impunity that hinders the free exercise of trade union rights.

Title: La Cantuta
CorteIDH: La Cantuta. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 20 de noviembre de 2009|La Cantuta. Sentencia de 29 de noviembre de 2006|Barrios Altos y La Cantuta. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 30 de Mayo de 2018|La Cantuta. Sentencia de 30 de noviembre de 2007|Barrios Altos y La Cantuta. Audiencia del 2 de febrero de 2018
CIDH: La Cantuta. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 42/99
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the illegal arrest, forced disappearance and extrajudicial execution of a professor and a group of students from the Enrique Guzmán y Valle National University in La Cantuta, Lima. This event took place at dawn on July 18, 1992 and was carried out by Peruvian army personnel and agents from the “Colina” group. This group, assigned to the National Intelligence Service, was responsible for the identification, control and elimination of those people who were suspected of belonging to insurgent or opposition groups to President Fujimori’s regime, through the systematic use of indiscriminate extrajudicial executions, mass murder, forced disappearances and torture. Investigations were opened which were processed in military courts, but the incidents remained in impunity, and this situation was reinforced by the application of amnesty laws. According to the interpretation of the IA Court, the events at La Cantuta were fostered by a generalized situation of impunity towards serious human rights violations of that period, favored and tolerated by the absence of judicial guarantees and the inefficiency of legal institutions to tackle systematic human rights violations. The IA Court applied standards relating to the forced disappearance of people and to the State’s obligation to investigate ex officio , without delay, and in a serious, impartial and effective manner.
Descriptores: Privación de libertad|Ejecución extrajudicial|Desaparición forzada|Jurisdicción militar

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the extrajudicial execution of Luis Alfredo Almonacid Arellano in September 1973, in the context of the military regime which governed Chile during that time. Investigations into the events were affected by the application of the amnesty law which was approved by legal Decree N° 2191 in 1978. The IA Court developed criteria for the definition of crimes against humanity and the obligation of states to investigate and punish crimes of this nature, regardless of the existence of amnesty laws. Furthermore, standards were developed with regards to the State obligation to ensure the exercise of “conventionality control” between domestic legal regulations and the American Convention.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the illegal detention, torture and forced disappearance of Agustín Goiburú Giménez, Carlos José Mancuello Bareiro and the brothers Rodolfo and Benjamín Ramírez Villalba, which occurred during the dictatorship of Alfredo Stroessner in Paraguay, in the context of the so-called “Operation Condor” - the name given to the alliance which united and combined the security forces and intelligence of services of Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia and Brazil. The IA Court consolidated its jurisprudence with regards to the continued and permanent character of the crime of forced disappearance, and recognized that said crime and the consequent obligation to investigate and sanction those responsible have the character of non-derogable standards of international law jus cogens. The IA Court also analyzed the dictatorial regime, including the scope of the obligation of interstate cooperation with regard to extradition.

Resumen: The events of the case relate to the extrajudicial execution of 37 inmates on November 27, 1992, in the Catia Detention Center, Caracas. The events occurred in a framework of serious civil riot at a national level and extreme political unrest, provoked by the second attempt at a coup d’état against the administration of the then President Carlos Andrés Pérez, carried out by a civilian-military group formed by high-ranking officers of the four branches of the Armed Forces and several civilian opponents. In this context, National Guard and Metropolitan Police Officers intervened the penitentiary and exercising excessive force, shot indiscriminately at the inmates, resulting in the death of more than 60 prisoners, 52 injured and 28 disappeared. Venezuela recognized its international responsibility for the reported events. The IA Court established standards regarding the use of force by State security bodies and regarding penitentiary conditions and the State’s obligation to guarantee the right to humane treatment.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the death of Bernabé Baldeón García, a 68 year old peasant, who was detained and tortured by military staff in the department of Ayacucho during the initial stages of the 1990s. The IA Court considered that during the 80s and towards the end of 2000, Peru experienced a conflict between armed groups and military and police agents. This conflict was exacerbated by the systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. The IA Court identified the deficiencies in the judicial investigation into the death and torture of the victim and the impunity in which the events remained.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the right to ancestral property in the territory of the indigenous community Sawhoyamaxa, as well as the grave living conditions arising from being settled at the edge of a national road in a situation of extreme poverty, without access to basic services such as nutrition, housing, education or health, among others. The IA Court ratified the content, given the right to indigenous collective property and the special significance that land has for indigenous groups as the fundamental basis of their culture, spiritual life, integrity and economic survival. The Court identified that, due to this close link, they are protected by article 21 of the American Convention. The IA Court established the responsibility of the State for not adopting measures against the conditions of poverty and the lack of access to basic services suffered by the Sawhoyamaxa Community, particularly children and the elderly.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the extrajudicial execution and torture suffered in September 1995 by 4 people, among them 2 minors, committed by members of the Public Security Forces of the State. The victims were detained illegally, despite the issuing of a release order by a judge. During their detention, they were kept incommunicado and were tortured, and one of them was victim of sexual violence. Their bodies were found in different locations on the public highway. The events remained in impunity. The IA Court located the events in the context of state violence marked by the victimization of children and young people in situations of social risk, who were accused of being involved in the “maras” or youth gangs. This pattern translates into violent deaths, which are then socially exhibited by leaving bodies exposed in public spaces. The State carried out a partial recognition of responsibility for the events. The IA Court established standards with regard to collective detentions, concerning their arbitrary and illegal nature and the obligation of special protection in relation to children found under state custody.

CIDH: Penal Castro Castro. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 43/01
Lugar de los hechos: Penal Miguel Castro Castro: 11° 59' 2" S, 76° 59' 20" W
Resumen: The events of instant case refer to the extrajudicial execution, torture and mistreatment of prisoners in the two pavilions of Miguel Castro Castro penitentiary, a maximum-security prison, who were mostly serving sentences for terrorist acts. The massacre that took place in May 1992 was developed under the protection of the so-called “Operativo Mudanza”. During the operation, State agents from both the police and army used weapons of war, tear gas bombs and immobilizing gas against the prisoners, initiating the action on the day of female visits to the prison. The survivors were forced to remain in the prison areas called “no-man’s land” and “admission,” lying face down on the ground, without shelter and receiving constant beatings and assaults for several days until their transfer to other penitentiaries. Once they were relocated, the beatings and malnutrition continued and many of the wounded did not receive adequate and timely medical attention. The IA Court established standards regarding the excessive use of force used in carrying out this operation, due to the torture and abuse which the prisoners were subjected to, and made special reference to gender violence. In this respect, the IA Court took into consideration the distinct way in which the events affected the women, noting that the way in which the State violated rights could also have had the objective of causing a social effect. Furthermore, the Court considered that during the 80s and towards the end of 2000, Peru experienced a conflict between armed groups and military and police officers. This conflict was exacerbated by a systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders.

CIDH: Masacre de Ituango. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 75/01
Resumen: The facts of this case concern the massacres that occurred in June 1996 and October 1997 in the small towns of La Granja and El Aro, respectively, in the Ituango province, Antioquia region. The selective murder of 19 farmers, among them 1 child and 3 women, was a result of the paramilitary incursion which took place in both small towns with the support and acquiescence of members of the security forces. Many of these people were tortured before being murdered, their homes were raided, and a large part of the town centre was destroyed, forcing the mass displacement of more than 700 rural people. The facts of this case illustrate the serious human rights violations suffered by the civil population in the framework of the Colombian Armed Conflict, as a result of the joint actions between paramilitary groups and security forces. In this regard, the IA Court specifically referred to the negative effects suffered by the population as a consequence of the destruction and burning of homes and the subsequent forced mass displacement that the victims suffered, and set a case law precedent regarding the right to honor and dignity and freedom from slavery and servitude. The IA Court determined the State’s responsibility for having favored the creation of “paramilitary” self-defense groups and thereby having created a situation of risk for its inhabitants and not having adopted the necessary nor sufficient measures to avoid the perpetration of these massacres.

CIDH: Palamara Iribarne. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 77/01
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the censure of the book “Ethics and the intelligence services”, written by Humberto Antonio Palamara Iribarne, in which he addresses aspects of military intelligence. On the basis of this book, the victim was subjected to criminal proceedings in a military court for the crimes of disobedience and contempt, because at the time of the events, the victim was a retired officer of the Chilean Navy. The IA Court expressed the incompatibility of military jurisdiction with the American Convention in terms of its jurisdiction to try civilians, the lack of independence and impartiality of the military courts, as well as the violation of judicial guarantees occurring through a process characterized by secrecy and inquisition. The Court also analyzed the criminal prosecution of the crime of contempt in the context of a democratic society, and its implications on the exercise of the right to freedom of thought and expression.

CIDH: Masacre de Pueblo Bello. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 41/02
Lugar de los hechos: Masacre de Pueblo Bello: 8° 5' 35" N, 76° 43' 37" W
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the incursion on January 14, 1990 in the small town of Pueblo Bello, Turbo province, Antioquia region, of the paramilitary group “Los Tangueros,” under the order of Fidel Castaño. The paramilitaries looted some of the dwellings and moved an undetermined number of men by force to the town’s square, where they were forced to lie face down. From a list of these men 43 farmers were selected, 3 of whom were minors. The people were tied, forced to get into two trucks and taken to a farm where a paramilitary chief met them. There, the farmers were interrogated and tortured. Of the 43 victims, 37 disappeared and 6 were extrajudicially executed. The events of the case occurred in the context of the Colombian armed conflict and particularly in the framework of expansion and territorial control by paramilitary groups, as a reaction to the guerrilla insurgency in the Urabá Antioqueño region. The IA Court developed standards regarding the State’s responsibility for the breach of duties of prevention and protection of the region’s inhabitants from the acts of paramilitary groups, which had been declared a zone of emergency and military operations. Additionally it established that the events of the case and the violation of access to justice remained in impunity.

CIDH: Huilca Tecse. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 55/98
Resumen: The events of the case relate to the extrajudicial execution, on December 18, 1992, of Pedro Huilca Tecse, a Peruvian trade union leader. The execution was perpetrated by members of the “Colina” group, a death squad linked to the Intelligence Services of the Peruvian military. The Court developed standards on the right to free association with others persons, without the intervention of public authorities to limit or obstruct the exercise of this right. Furthermore, the Court interpreted the execution of a trade union leader to represent not only a restriction on the freedom of association of the individual, but also an affectation on the rights and liberty of a certain group to associate freely and without fear. The Court concluded that the facts of the case had an intimidating effect on workers in the Peruvian trade union movement, limiting the ability of this group to exercise said right.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the paramilitary incursion and the massacre of 49 rural farmers by paramilitaries, with the collaboration and acquiescence of members of the National Army, between July 15 and 20, 1997, in the province of Mapiripán, Meta region. The victims were detained, tortured, executed and/or disappeared, which led to a mass displacement of the region’s inhabitants. The IA Court developed standards regarding the State’s responsibility for the acts of individuals in cases of actions or failure to act by State agents in the position of guarantors of the obligations to respect and protect. Additionally, it highlighted the value of the standards of international humanitarian law for the interpretation of the American Convention, and it referred to the special State obligations relating to children in a situation of domestic armed conflict, given their particular vulnerability. It also extended its jurisprudence on the content and scope of the right to movement and residence, in relation to the forced displacement suffered by the victims and the wide range of rights that are affected as a consequence.

CIDH: López Álvarez. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 124/01
Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the deprivation of liberty of Alfredo López Álvarez, who was president of the “Comité de Defensa de Tierras Triunfeñas” [Committtee for the Defense of Triunfeñas Lands], and vice-president of the “Organización Fraternal Negra de Honduras” [Black Fraternal Organization of Honduras], after being detained by agents of the State for the alleged crime of drugs trafficking. After being transferred to the Criminal Investigation Division he suffered torture and was coerced into incriminating himself. He was eventually acquitted, however was detained for a further 7 months. The IA Court made reference to standards on preventative prison, the right to effective judicial remedy, and reasonable time period. In conjunction, it developed standards on the right to issue information, which in this case was damaged by the orders of the Director of the prison where the victim was kept; the prohibition of the right of the Garifuna population to speak in their mother tongue constituted a discriminatory act against him.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the arbitrary and illegal detention of Daniel Tibi in November 1995, as well as the torture and cruel, inhumane and degrading treatment which he suffered while he was deprived of liberty for the alleged crime of trafficking. The IA Court established the responsibility of the State for the violation of the right to judicial protection in detriment of the workers as a result of the municipal opposition to the execution of the sentences.In this sense, the Court understood that the execution of sentences must be considered an integral part of the right to access an effective remedy, and said execution must include full compliance with the respective decision.

Title: Acosta Calderón
CorteIDH: Acosta Calderón. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 7 de febrero de 2008|Acosta Calderón. Sentencia de 24 de junio de 2005
Resumen: The facts of the case concern the detention of Colombian national Rigoberto Acosta Calderón on suspicion of drug trafficking by Military Customs Police in November 1998. The IA Court established standards regarding pretrial detention in relation to the right to the presumption of innocence, as well as determining other violations of judicial guarantees linked to the reasonable time period of the criminal process, the right of the accused to be brought immediately before a competent judge and to informed in a detailed manner with regards to the accusations with which they are charged. Finally, the IA Court made reference to the right to consular assistance of foreign persons who are detained.

Carpio was a prominent politician and journalist, founder of the National Centrist Union party, and thereby opposition to the government. Resumen: The events of the case refer to the arbitrary arrest of María Teresa De La Cruz Flores, and her sentence for a terrorist crime without due process. The victim was arrested as she was finishing her work as a pediatrician and was prosecuted under terrorist charges by a court comprised of “faceless” judges, which sentenced her under the crime of terrorism to 20 years in prison. The Court analyzed the compatibility of the sentence with the principle of legality and of freedom from ex post facto laws, and established standards regarding the duty of doctors to safeguard the confidentiality of information which they have access to in their professional practice.

CIDH: Yakye Axa. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 02/02
Lugar de los hechos: Comunidad Indígena Yakye Axa: 23° 31' 13" S, 58° 44' 44" W
Resumen: The facts of the case concern the right to ancestral property of the indigenous community Yakye Axa, as well as the grave conditions of life in which its members were found as a consequence of being placed at the edge of a national road in a situation of extreme poverty and without access to basic services such as nutrition, housing, education or health, among others. The IA Court recognized the right to collective indigenous property, developing the special significance which ancestral territories have for indigenous communities, as the fundamental basis of their culture, spiritual life, integrity and economic survival. As a result of this close link, they are protected by article 21 of the American Convention. The IA Court also evidenced the State’s responsibility for not adopting measures to address the poor conditions and lack of access to basic services which the Yakye Axa Community experienced, in particular children and the elderly. The IA Court explicitly recognized that the traditional possession indigenous groups maintain of their lands has an equivalent effect to the title of full ownership granted by the State. As a consequence, those who for reasons outside of their control have left or lost possession of their lands retain the right of ownership over them, despite the absence of legal title when said lands are found to be under private ownership. Similarly, it established that in order to guarantee the rights of the indigenous communities, States must interpret and apply the standards, taking into account the particular characteristics which shape their cultural identity.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the alleged illegal detention and torture of Alfonso Martín del Campo Dodd as perpetrated by the Judicial Police of Mexico’s Distrito Federal, and his sentence to 50 years in prison for double homicide based on a confession obtained under torture. The IA Court upheld the non jurisdiction objection for ratione temporis requested by the State. To this end, it referenced the State’s duty to investigate, prosecute and punish those responsible for the denounced events. However it recognised that the acts of torture were not continuous, but an instantaneous offence, thereby it does not have jurisdiction to hear a case, once the events have occurred prior to the recognition of the IA Court’s jurisdiction.

CIDH: Herrera Ulloa. Informe de Admisibilidad N° 128/01
Resumen: The facts of the case concern the criminal conviction imposed on the journalist Mauricio Herrero Ulloa for defamation, and the civil conviction imposed upon both the journalist and the newspaper “La Nación” for compensation of moral damages following the publication of a series of journalistic articles in which a Cost Rican diplomat was linked to the carrying out of diverse illegal activities. The IA Court analyzed the validity of the criminalization of the crimes of defamation, calumny, and slander when questions of public interest regarding public functionaries are being addressed. The IA Court identified the particular importance of the freedom of expression in a democratic society, and determined the content of this right as well as the terms upon which its restrictions should be analyzed. Furthermore, the IA Court developed standards and determined the content of the right to appeal, establishing that this presupposes the existence of an extensive legal resource which permits the Court to carry out a comprehensive and integral analysis of all issues debated and analyzed in the lower tribunal.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the massacre of 268 people in July 1982. The majority were members of the Mayan indigenous community of Plan de Sánchez, executed by members of the Guatemalan military, and the acts remained in impunity due to the lack of an effective investigation. After these events, the families of the victims and survivors of the massacre were subject to acts of intimidation and discrimination. The IA Court placed the events of the case in the context of the internal armed conflict that occurred in Guatemala between 1962 and 1996, during which the “National Security Doctrine” was applied. The Mayan people were considered to be the “internal enemy.” The State acknowledged complete international responsibility for the aforementioned acts.

Title: Lori Berenson Mejía
CorteIDH: Lori Berenson Mejía. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 22 de septiembre de 2006|Lori Berenson Mejía. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 20 de junio de 2012|Lori Berenson Mejía. Sentencia de 23 de junio de 2005|Lori Berenson Mejía. Sentencia de 25 de noviembre de 2004
CIDH: Lori Berenson Mejía. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 56/98
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the arrest and subsequent prosecution pursuant to Peruvian anti-terrorist legislation by a “faceless” military court and with restrictions to Lori Helene Berenson Mejía’s right to defense. The victim was condemned to a life sentence for the crime of treason. As a result of the defense’s filing of a motion for special review, the verdict was quashed and the case transferred to the ordinary criminal court. Ultimately, Lori Berenson’s responsibility for the crime of collaborating with terrorists was established and she was sentenced to 20 years imprisonment. The IA Court considered that the context in which the events developed correspond to the period when Peru experienced a conflict between armed groups and military and police officers, during the 80s and towards the end of 2000. This conflict was exacerbated by a systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. The IA Court commented on the detention conditions suffered by the victim (prolonged isolation, coercive solitary confinement, poor diet, poor sanitary conditions, restrictions on her visitation rights and deficient medical attention, amongst others), which was considered as cruel, inhumane, and degrading treatment in violation of the American Convention. The IA Court reiterated the components relating to the need to observe the principle of legality in the formulation of criminal definitions and the illegality of military criminal jurisdiction in crimes committed by civilians due to the breach of the right to a natural judge and due process, both guarantees associated with the right to access to justice.

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the grave conditions of detention to which children were subjected in the “Instituto de Reeducación del Menor “Panchito López”” [Institute of Reeducation of the Minor “Panchito López”] between the years 1996 and 2011. In particular, it concerns the damages caused by three fires which occurred in the years 2000 and 2001, in which 12 children died and dozens were left injured. The IA Court analyzed the violations of the right to life and personal integrity in light of the additional and specific obligations which children’s rights, enshrined in article 19 of the American Convention, impose upon States. The IA Court focused on the content and scope of these rights, taking into consideration the pertinent dispositions of the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Additional Protocol on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, which alongside the American Convention, constitute an international corpus juris of child protection which States must respect. Similarly, the IA Court recognized that when addressing judicial proceedings in which children’s rights are discussed, and in particular when a child is subjected to a criminal proceeding, the exercise of judicial guarantees enshrined in article 8 of the American Convention involves the adoption of specific and particular measures.

CIDH: Hermanos Gómez Paquiyauri. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 44/01
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the arbitrary arrest, torture and extrajudicial execution of brothers Emilio Moisés and Rafael Samuel Gómez Paquiyauri, 14 and 17 years old, respectively, on June 21, 1991 by National Police officers. These acts took place as part of an operation that was searching for people involved in alleged terrorist attacks, as part of a plan known as “Cerco Noventiuno.” These events occurred in the context of conflict between armed groups and military and police officers, which took place in Peru during the 80s and towards the end of 2000. This conflict was exacerbated by a systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. The IA Court highlighted the framework of impunity associated with the case, as a consequence of which the perpetrators of the lowest rank in the Peruvian National Police were prosecuted and convicted, at the same time that the actual mastermind or masterminds were not prosecuted and only one has been allegedly identified. The IA Court emphasized that, given that the victims were children, the events are marked by a particular gravity. In this regard, the State’s obligation to respect the right to life of every person under its jurisdiction presents special conditions in the case of minors and becomes an obligation to prevent situations that could lead, whether by act or omission, to its infringement.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the arbitrary detention and torture of Maritza Urrutia Garcia due to her connection with the insurgency group, the Guerrilla Army of the Poor (EGP), in July 1992. After her arrest, the victim was held in a clandestine detention center for 8 days and forced to issue a communiqué to the public, which her captors had previously prepared. Mrs Urrutia subsequently left the country and obtained refugee status in Mexico. The IA Court placed the events in the context of internal armed conflict at beginning of the process of peace negotiations between the government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit, evidencing the Army’s practice of capturing guerrilla fighters and secretly detaining and torturing them in order to obtain useful information. The IA Court established standards regarding the situation of illegally detained persons and concerning the prohibition of torture in circumstances of internal armed conflict, and evidenced that the acts have remained in impunity.

Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the forced disappearance of 19 people dedicated to commercial activities in the province of Puerto Boyacá, carried out by the paramilitary group, “Asociación de Campesinos y Ganaderos del Magdalena Medio” (ACDEGAM)] who controlled the region of Magdalena Medio with the support of the State’s military forces. Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the illegal detention of 17 year old Walter Bulacio during a mass detention, a practice known as “Razzia” and protected by active legal regulations in the city of Buenos Aires. The mass detention was carried out in the area where a rock concert was due to take place. Bulacio was taken to a police station where he was held in solitary confinement, without being informed of the reasons for his detention and without being brought before a judge. The young man was beaten by police agents and died a few days after as a consequence of the injuries incurred.

Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the extrajudicial execution of 15 people, who were residents in the Barrios Altos neighborhood in Lima city, by 6 heavily armed individuals. Upon entering the place, the attackers fired indiscriminately, they then fled the scene in 2 vehicles. Judicial investigations and journalist reports revealed that those responsible worked for military intelligence and were members of the Peruvian army who served in the Colina Group. Despite the fact that the events took place in 1991, the judicial authorities only opened a serious investigation into the incident in April 1995, which was interrupted by a complaint of competence from the military court presented before the High Court for the reason that the events related to military personnel in active service. Before the Court could resolve the matter, the Congress passed an Amnesty law, which exonerated military personnel, police and civilians of responsibility, who had committed or participated in human rights violations between 1980 and 1995. The effect of this law was to determine the definitive closing of judicial proceedings and thereby avoid criminal responsibility for those responsible for the massacre. The IA Court declared that the Amnesty law was incompatible with the American Convention.

CIDH: Tribunal Constitucional. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 35/98
Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the dismissal of 3 magistrates from the Constitutional Court who were impeached by Congress. The impeachment was based on the non application of Act no. 26,657, which enabled a second Presidential re-election and which allowed the then President Alberto Fujimori to run for a third consecutive term. Following these events, the victims filed a writ of amparo against the dismissal decisions, which were rejected by Lima’s High Court of Justice and subsequently confirmed by the Constitutional Court. As a consequence of these procedures, the victims suffered a series of harassments and persecutions from the Peruvian authorities. The IA Court referred to the institution of impeachment and guarantees of due process of law and requirement of the judge’s impartiality.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the judicial censorship of the screening of the film “The Last Temptation of Christ”, on the grounds that it was offensive to the figure of Christ and therefore negatively affected Catholics. The Chilean Political Constitution establishes a system for the censorship of advertising and film. The IA Court established two dimensions which form the basis of the right to freedom of expression. The first dimension establishes the right to utilize any means appropriate to disseminate thought and allow it to reach the greatest audience possible, and as such recognises the indivisible nature of the expression and dissemination of thought and information. The second dimension is of a social character; recognising that freedom of speech is a means for the interchange of ideas and information between people and therefore also addresses the right of all individuals to receive opinions, news and reports. Both dimensions are equally important, and should be simultaneously guaranteed in order to ensure full effectiveness of the right to freedom of thought and expression.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the massacre of 251 inhabitants, women, men and children, from the community of “Las Dos Erres,” which occurred on 6th to 8th December 1982 and was perpetrated by members of the specialized group within the armed force called “Kaibiles”. Judicial investigations were initiated more than 10 years after the events. The IA Court evaluated the legal proceedings in light of the standards of due diligence, referring specifically to the pattern of sexual violence used against women in contexts of armed conflict. Furthermore, it focused on the State’s obligation to provide children with special protection, regarding the systematic pattern of illegal abduction and detention of minors perpetrated and tolerated by agents of the State at the time of the events.

Resumen: The events concern the extrajudicial execution of 6 unarmed rural farmers, in the province of Las Palmeras, Putumayo region, by members of the National Police and Army. The case also addresses the lack of administration of justice, which meant that the events remained in impunity. The IA Court advanced in its jurisprudence regarding the responsibility of States for the violations of the rights to a fair trial and to judicial protection as a consequence of the use of military jurisdiction in cases of serious human rights’ violations, as this jurisdiction violates the right to a competent, impartial and independent judge. Additionally, the IA Court evidenced the violation of rights as a consequence of the excessive time period the ordinary criminal process lasted without having identified or punished those responsible for the extrajudicial execution, which violates the limits of a reasonable time period.

Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the arrest, prosecution and judgment of Gustavo Adolfo Cesti Hurtado, a retired army officer who was brought before the military court for crimes against military duty and fraud. Resumen: The facts of the case relate to the prosecution and sentence to life imprisonment of 4 Chilean citizens for the crime of treason considered in Peruvian legislation as a form of aggravated terrorism. The Court understood that during the 80s and towards the end of 2000, Peru experienced a conflict between armed groups and military and police officers. This conflict was exacerbated by a systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. The IA Court considered the victims’ prosecution and sentence in the military court by a “faceless” tribunal, and the lack of precision in the definition of the criminal charges of terrorism and treason with which they were convicted, and affected their legal status in the enforceable penalty, the presiding court and the corresponding proceedings, resulted in the violation of their right to defense and the principal of legality.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the extrajudicial execution of a group of 5 young people living on the streets, 3 of them being minors. 4 of the victims were previously abducted and tortured. The IA Court located the events within the context of the state’s practice to use state security forces to threaten, arrest, perpetrate cruel, inhumane and degrading treatment and murder against “street children” as a means of counteracting juvenile delinquency. The IA Court applied standards of protection for the right to life, inclusive of the guarantee to a dignified life, emphasizing the risks which “street children” are exposed to. Furthermore, it applied criteria of a complete analysis of the internal process in order to resolve the State’s failure to comply with their obligation to investigate the facts adequately and effectively.

Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the forced disappearance of Efraín Bámaca Velásquez, commander of the guerilla group Organization of People in Arms (ORPA), after being captured in March 1992, by Army officers. During his captivity, Mr. Bámaca Velásquez was subjected to torture. The IA Court placed these events in the context of the internal armed conflict that occurred in Guatemala, exposing the army’s practice of capturing guerillas and keeping them in clandestine detention in order to obtain information from them by means of torture. The State recognized its international responsibility for violating State obligation to respect and guarantee the rights established in the American Convention. Notwithstanding, the IA Court developed standards regarding the nature of forced disappearance as a violation of multiple rights and a violation of the victim’s and family’s right to personal integrity

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the illegal deprivation of liberty of Luis Alberto Cantoral Benavides, following his arbitrary imprisonment, torture, the violation of his judicial guarantees and the double jeopardy imposed as a result of the mentioned events. The victim was detained by agents of the Counter Terrorism Division (DINCOTE) in February 1993, during which time a state of constitutional emergency was in place involving the suspension of a series of guarantees. During his detention, he was subjected to acts of violence whose objective was to obtain self-incrimination. These events occurred in the context of the armed conflict experienced in Peru between armed groups and military and police agents during the 1980s and until the end of 2000. This conflict was exacerbated by the systematic practice of human rights violations, among them extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances of people suspected of belonging to opposition political groups, which were carried out by State agents following orders of police and military leaders. Mr. Cantoral Benavides was subjected to legal proceedings in a military court, which according to the IA Court’s analysis violated the requirements of independence and impartiality established in the American Convention. The IA Court also evaluated the compatibility of the criminal definition of terrorism and treason with the principle that penalties must be lawful.

Title: Durand y Ugarte

Sentencia de 16 de agosto de 2000|Durand y Ugarte. Sentencia de 28 de mayo de 1999|Durand y Ugarte. Sentencia de 3 de diciembre de 2001|Durand y Ugarte. Audiencia del 2 de febrero de 2018
Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the illegal arrest, by members of the Counter-Terrorism Office (DIRCOTE), and the disappearance of Norberto Durand Ugarte and Gabriel Pablo Ugarte Rivera, under the suspicion of having participated in terrorist acts, without a warrant or having being found guilty of any felony. Whilst the victims were being detained, there was a riot in the “El Frontón” prison, which was declared as a “restricted military zone,” in this way preventing the entry of judicial and civil authorities. During the operation to recover control of the prison, security forces demolished the Blue Pavilion causing injury and death amongst the prisoners. Durand and Ugarte were not on the list of survivors nor were their corpses identified. Regarding the violation of humane treatment, the IA Court established that is it not possible to infer the practice of torture or cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment from the disproportionate use of force employed to overthrow the riot, given that such concepts possess their own legal nature. The Court further stated that such concepts do not necessarily and automatically conclude in the arbitrary deprivation of life, even in circumstances such as those of this case.
Descriptores: Privación de libertad|Ejecución extrajudicial|Tortura y tratos crueles, inhumanos o degradantes|Uso de la fuerza

Resumen: The facts of the case concern the illegal and arbitrary detention, in June 1992, of Rafael Suárez Rosero on the part of Ecuadorian National Police agents. This occurred in the context of the police operation “Ciclón”, whose objective was to break up one of the biggest international drug trafficking organizations. The victim was detained without a warrant having been emitted by a competent authority and without having committed delicto flagrante. Following several days kept in isolation, he was remanded in custody by a judge. The IA Court established standards on preventative detention as a precautionary and not punitive measure, further defining isolation as a measure of exceptional nature. The Court also ratified the extent to which habeas corpus should be understood.

Resumen: The events of the case relate to the kidnapping and subsequent disappearance of Ernesto Rafael Castillo Páez by the Peruvian National Police in October 1990, in the context of an operation to arrest those in charge of the group “Sendero Luminoso”. After the victim’s disappearance, the relatives filed a writ of habeas corpus, which subsequently led to criminal proceedings for the crime of abuse of authority against various Police officials. Nevertheless, the court ordered for the case to be closed without anyone being punished. The IA Court considered the incidents from the perspective of forced disappearance, furthermore establishing the relevance of habeas corpus in these types of cases. In the same way, the IA Court noted that the State is obligated to investigate these types of events given that even if difficulties of an internal nature prevent the identification of those responsible, the victim’s family still has the right to know what happened to the victim and the whereabouts of his remains.

Resumen: The events of the case relate to the arrest of María Elena Loayza Tamayo by the Counter Terrorism Division (DINCOTE) due to an alleged association and collaboration with the group “Sendero Luminoso”. After her arrest she was held incommunicado for 10 days and was subjected to torture, cruel and degrading treatment and sexual violence, all with the purpose of self-incrimination. In light of her refusal, she was prosecuted for the crime of treason and tried by various military courts, which finally absolved her of all charges. Nevertheless, at the moment of passing the case to the civil court, the victim was convicted to a term of 20 years imprisonment by a Special “faceless” Court for the crime of terrorism. During the entire proceedings, both in the military and civil courts, the victim was kept in detention. The IA Court brought to attention that in this case the article of Decree-Law 25,659 under which she was prosecuted, prevented the victim from using habeas corpus to safeguard her personal liberty or to question the legality of her arrest.

Resumen: The facts of this case account for the forced disappearance of Isidro Caballero Delgado and María del Carmen Santana, who were arrested in February 1989 by the Colombian Army’s patrol and by various civilians who were collaborating with them, in the province of San Alberto, Cesar region. Resumen: The facts of the case concern the disappearance of the Costa Rican nationals Francisco Fairén Garbi and Yolanda Solís Corrales, while they travelled through Honduras towards Mexico. The IA Court developed standards on forced disappearances, invoking the cases Velásquez Rodríguez and Godínez Cruz in their decisions. However, the case was rejected because it wasn’t considered to be evidenced that the disappearance of the victims was related with the active State practice of forced disappearance at the time of the events.

Title: Velásquez Rodríguez
CorteIDH: Velásquez Rodríguez. Sentencia de 21 de julio de 1989|Velásquez Rodríguez. Sentencia de 26 de junio de 1987|Velásquez Rodríguez. Sentencia de 29 de julio de 1988|Velásquez Rodríguez. Sentencia de 17 de agosto de 1990
Jueces firmantes: Rafael Nieto Navia|Rodolfo Piza Escalante|Rigoberto Espinal Irías|Héctor Gross Espiell|Pedro Nikken|Héctor Fix Zamudio
Resumen: The facts of the case refer to the forced disappearance of Manfredo Velásquez Rodríguez, a university student kidnapped by agents of the State in September 1982. Such acts occurred in a time in which disappearances constituted a systematic practice utilized on those persons considered dangerous for the security of the State. This is the first sentence issued by the IA Court, and as such establishes important standards regarding the legal nature and the elements of forced disappearance as a multiple and continued violation of numerous rights contained in the Convention, alongside the development of the content of the state obligations with regards to respect, guarantee and adaptation of domestic law, as well as the scope of the obligations to prevent, investigate, sanction and provide reparations of all violation of rights.

Title: Godínez Cruz
CorteIDH: Godínez Cruz. Sentencia de 17 de agosto de 1990|Godínez Cruz. Sentencia de 21 de julio de 1989|Godínez Cruz. Sentencia de 20 de enero de 1989|Godínez Cruz. Sentencia de 26 de junio de 1987
Resumen: The facts of the case concern the forced disappearance of Saúl Godínez Cruz in July 1982, while he was ON HIS WAY TO WORK as a teacher/ while he was on his way to teach. The victim was an active union leader and had participated in various strikes initiated in that/this period. The IA Court applied the standards developed in the case of Velásquez Rodríguez regarding the elements and characteristics of forced disappearance, taking into consideration the prevailing historical context at the time of the events. Equally, the IA Court established standards developing the characteristics of obligation through the state duty to prevent and sanction.

Title: Masacre Plan de Sánchez
Relacionado: Masacre Plan de Sánchez (Salvador Jerónimo y otros). Resolución del Presidente de 30 de julio de 2004

It also concerns their participation - as witnesses or observers - at a public hearing around the Massacre Plan de Sánchez case held at the Inter-American Court. In 2006, the Inter-American Court extended the protection measures to cover the members of the Community Studies and Psychosocial Action Team (Asociación Civil Equipo de Estudios Comunitarios y Acción Psicosocial, ECAP), which supports the reparation process for the victims and survivors of the Massacre Plan de Sánchez case.

Carlos Dunshee de Abrantes
Ibsen Cárdenas e Ibsen Peña
CorteIDH: Ibsen Cárdenas e Ibsen Peña. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 14 de Octubre de 2014
Resumen: The request for provisional measures to protect the life and personal integrity of members of the Ibsen family and their representative is based on facts that concern harassment and threats, as well delays in the payment of damages. It also refers to the procedures used to identify remains exhumed in October 2012, per a judgment handed down to Bolivia on September 1, 2010 for the forced disappearance of Rainer Ibsen Cárdenas and José Luis Ibsen Pena. The Inter-American Court rejected the request for provisional measures because it considered that the requirements of extreme gravity, urgency and irreparable damage were not met; the Inter-American Court issued its assessment within the context of monitoring the implementation of the sentence.

Resumen: The request for protection of the personal integrity of Mr. Cesti Hurtado concern the adequate medical treatment necessary for his heart conditions. In June 1999, an extension in favor of members of his family (who were harassed and threatened for Mr. Cesti Hurtado’s work before the inter-American system) was requested and approved. Title: Acevedo Jaramillo
CorteIDH: Acevedo Jaramillo y otros. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 23 de noviembre de 2004|Acevedo Jaramillo y otros. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 28 de agosto de 2015|Acevedo Jaramillo y otros. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 19 de noviembre de 2020
Resumen: The petition for protection is based on the opening of an investigation and the issuing of an arrest warrant for the purpose of intimidating the victims, their representatives, and witnesses of the case for having filed a claim before human rights protection bodies. The Inter-American Court rejected the request because it considered that the requirements of extreme gravity and urgency were not met. In May of 2015, a new request was submitted to protect workers who were returned into Lima’s city hall workforce and who suffered various forms of ill-treatment. The Inter-American Court did not accept the request as it considered it to be within the realm of compliance monitoring of the merits ruling. In October 2020, new provisional measures in favor of Mrs. Liliana Cerff Ascama, one of the victims of the case, were requested in order to call for the immediate compliance with the payment obligations still due in light of her critical health condition. The IA Court declared the request without merit on the grounds that it pertains to the process of supervision of the execution of the judgment.

Title: Hermanas Serrano Cruz
Relacionado: Hermanas Serrano Cruz. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 6 de abril de 2006|El Salvador
Resumen: The request seeks to protect José Mario Sánchez González, a Nicaraguan national and a member of the organization "Pro-Search Association" (Asociación Pro Búsqueda) which searches for children who disappeared during the Salvadoran armed conflict. The request concerns a citation issued in March 2006 by the General Directorate of Migrations of El Salvador regarding his illegal stay in the country. This situation is related to the criticisms voiced by the “Pro-Search Association” within the context of follow-up to the implementation of the Inter-American Court’s ruling in the case of the Serrano Cruz Sisters, in which the organization acts as legal representatives of the victims. The purpose of the request was to order El Salvador to refrain from any possible deportation until José Mario Sánchez González’s temporary residency renewal process is resolved. The petitioner withdrew his petition before the Inter-American Court resolved the case.

Resumen: The request for protection concerns Wenceslaus James, Anthony Briggs, Noel Anderson, Anthony Garcia and Christopher Bethel (among others) who face the death penalty in Trinidad and Tobago. The protective measures seek to halt the executions and to ensure that the state does not violate a potential future decision by the organs of the inter-American system around its responsibility to protect the right to life, as well as to allow for adequate reparations. In April 2009, the Inter-American Court decided to lift the protection measures for a group of beneficiaries, establishing that the follow-up would be within monitoring compliance with the merits sentence in the Hilaire, Constantine, Benjamín and others Case. In that same procedural step, the Inter-American Court decided to maintain protection in favor of a group of seven victims, ordering to change the name of the case to “Dottin et al”. Finally, the Inter-American Court lifted all the measures in April 2013, closing the entire process.

Resolución de la CorteIDH de 18 de junio de 2005
CIDH: Penitenciarias de Mendoza. Informe de Admisibilidad Nº 70/05
Resumen: The request for provisional measures was submitted by the Inter-American Commission, based on its precautionary measures MC 923-04, and due to the gravity of the prison situation of the Provincial Prison of Mendoza and of the Gustavo André Unit in the town of Lavalle. The evidence highlighted the continued risk to the lives of inmates, various incidents that led to inmates killed/injured and employees injured, as well as deplorable living conditions in detention centers, among other issues. The Inter-American Court ordered the State to adopt the necessary measures to protect the life and integrity of people deprived of liberty in the aforementioned prisons, as well as of all people within these units, and to investigate the acts of violence upon which the peition is based. In December 2010, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights lifted these measures. The following year, in 2011, the Inter-American Court rejected a new request that sought to extend protection to other units, stating that "the inter-American human rights system will continue to address the situation of the Mendoza Prisons through the actions of one of its organs [the Inter-American Commission], which must determine the next step in the proceedings, either within the framework of the petition pending definition, or by means of other mechanisms such as the Inter-American Commission’s Rapporteur for the Rights of Persons Deprived of Liberty”.

Title: Penal Miguel Castro Castro

Resolución de la CorteIDH de 30 de enero de 2007|Penal Castro Castro. Resolucion de la CorteIDH de 29 de julio de 2020|Penal Castro Castro. Resolución de la CorteIDH de 23 de marzo de 2021
Resumen: The request for provisional measures is based on facts surrounding the harassment and impact upon the honor of the victims of the case of the Miguel Castro Castro Prison through the publication of articles in the media. The arrest warrant issued against Mónica Feria Tinta was included, but the Inter-American Court considered that this had not been a part of the facts discussed within the the Castro Castro Prison case. The Inter-American Court rejected the request because it considered that it did not meet the minimum requirement of extreme gravity and urgency. In December 2007, the victims reiterated their request for protection and the Court again rejected the request. In December of 2017, the victims presented a new request for protection in the context of the pardon given to former President Alberto Fujimori. The Inter-American Court dismissed the request.

Title: Gomes Lund y otros (Guerrilha de Araguaia)
Relacionado: Gomes Lund e outros (Guerrilha de Araguaia). Resolución de la CorteIDH de 15 de julio de 2009
Resumen: The facts of the request for protective measures refer to an administrative resolution by the Brazilian Ministry of Defense, which created a Working Group to locate and identify the mortal remains of those who presumably have died during a combat known as ‘Guerrilha do Araguaia’. These provisional measures address the risk that this Working Group posed on future compliance with a potential reparation measure to adequately investigate the facts in the Guerilha do Araguaia case, which was pending before the Inter-American System. The Inter-American Court rejected the petition because it considered - among other factors - that the changes made by the State to the group originally established avoided a situation of extreme gravity and irreparable damage.
